MEXICO CITY, Mexico (CNN) -- The driver of a truck that collided with a bus in northeast Mexico, killing 12 people including 11 passengers from the United States and Canada, was intoxicated, a Mexican official said Tuesday. Emergency workers wheel a crash victim on a gurney after Monday's bus crash in Mexico. The tractor-trailer's 21-year-old driver was among those hospitalized after Monday's crash near Monterrey, Mexico, said Segismundo Doguin Martinez, a police official in the Mexican state of Coahuila. The driver of the bus was among those killed, and 15 bus passengers were injured. The Senda Express bus, operated by Grupo Senda, had been traveling from McAllen, Texas, carrying tourists to Zacatecas in central Mexico. Eight of those who died were from the United States, three were from Canada and one, the bus driver, was from Mexico, Doguin said.  Watch rescuers work at scene of deadly crash » . The survivors, most of them in grave condition, were taken to the Christus Muguerza Hospital and the Clinica La Concepcion, the Mexican official said. "They are in a delicate state but out of danger," Doguin said. El Milenio newspaper reported on its Web site that eight of the injured are from the United States, four are from Canada and three from Mexico. Seven of the injured Americans are from Texas and one is from Iowa, the newspaper said. El Norte newspaper's Web site and El Porvenir said the dead and injured included tourists. Among those killed in the crash was 73-year-old Ronald Christy, said his daughter, Pam Fordyce. Christy's wife, Margaret Christy, was in critical condition in a Mexican hospital, Fordyce said. "He was doing exactly what he loved -- traveling," Fordyce, of Altoona, Iowa, told CNN by telephone Tuesday. "He was right where he would want to be, on a bus." She said the couple wintered in Texas and lived in West Liberty, Iowa, in the summer. The U.S. consulate called her at 1:30 a.m. Tuesday to tell her that her father had been killed, Fordyce said, and then followed up with an e-mail with photographs of the crash. "I didn't even know he was on a bus," she said. "I guess I could believe [the consulate] when I talked to my brother" who knew the couple was traveling, she said. "Until then you don't want to believe anything." Doguin, the Mexican official, said the accident occurred when a truck driver went off the road and then overcorrected and swerved into oncoming traffic, hitting the bus. Video of the scene from CNN affiliate TV Azteca 13 showed the left side of the bus sheared off and the semi's cab completely flattened. Rescue efforts took five hours, TV Azteca 13 reported. The U.S. consulate in Monterrey will not release the names of the dead or injured until all family members have been notified, said consulate spokesman Todd Huizinga. "On Monday evening, staff from the consulate in Monterrey went to the Christus Muguerza Hospital to offer assistance to some of the injured who were brought there after the crash," Huizinga said. "The consulate expects to have more detail in the coming hours." The truck driver was injured and is being held by authorities at a hospital, Doguin said. The Web site for Grupo Senda says the company started in Linares, Mexico, more than 75 years ago. It provides bus service to 15 Mexican states and the Texas Valley, the site says. Elizabeth Suarez, director of the McAllen Central Bus Station, where the bus trip originated, issued a statement saying, "We are very saddened by the news this morning. We offer our condolences to the families. The city of McAllen is the landlord of the bus terminal facility in McAllen. Grupo Senda is our tenant." CNN's Melanie Whitley, Taylor Gandossy, Tess Eastment and Monica Trevino contributed to this report from Atlanta, Georgia.

**At least 12 dead, including US and Canadian tourists, after tour bus crashes in Mexico**

**By CNN Staff**
Updated 8:15 AM EDT, Wednesday, May 15, 2024

**(CNN) —** A tropical vacation turned into tragedy on Tuesday when a tour bus carrying foreign tourists flipped over on a highway in eastern Mexico, leaving at least 12 people dead—including American and Canadian citizens—and 18 others injured, according to local authorities.

The crash occurred shortly after 2:00 p.m. local time on Federal Highway 307, a major thoroughfare connecting the resort town of Tulum to the Mayan ruins of Coba in the state of Quintana Roo. 

The bus, operated by a local excursion company, was carrying 31 passengers who were returning from a day trip to the ancient archaeological site.

### Preliminary investigation points to mechanical failure

According to the Quintana Roo State Secretariat of Public Security, preliminary reports indicate the crash was caused by a sudden tire blowout while the vehicle was traveling at high speed during a heavy rainstorm. The driver reportedly lost control on the slick asphalt, causing the bus to veer off the road, strike a guardrail, and overturn into dense brush along the shoulder.

Emergency responders, including local police, paramedics, and the Mexican Red Cross, rushed to the scene to extract passengers trapped inside the wreckage.

"The scene was chaotic," said Captain Eduardo Martin of the Quintana Roo State Fire Department. "Rain was pouring down, and several passengers were pinned beneath the vehicle. Our primary focus was rapid triage and stabilizing those with severe trauma."

Mexican federal prosecutors announced that an official investigation has been launched into the bus company to determine whether the vehicle met safety standards and if mechanical negligence played a role. The driver survived the crash with minor injuries and is currently in custody as authorities investigate.

### Devastated families seek answers

As news of the crash broke, distraught family members in North America scrambled for updates on their loved ones.

Mark Miller, a resident of Columbus, Ohio, confirmed that his sister, 34-year-old Sarah Miller, was among those who lost their lives in the crash. Sarah had been celebrating her fifth wedding anniversary with her husband, David, who remains in critical condition at a hospital in Playa del Carmen.

"We went from looking at photos of them having the time of their lives to getting a horrific phone call from the embassy," an emotional Miller told CNN via phone. "Sarah was vibrant, full of life, and loved traveling. We are completely heartbroken, and we just want David to wake up. We also want to know why this bus was on the road if it wasn't safe."

In Montreal, Canada, the Tremblay family is mourning the loss of 62-year-old Jean-Pierre Tremblay, a retired teacher who was traveling with a group of friends. 

"My father worked his whole life and was finally enjoying his retirement," his daughter, Chantal Tremblay, said in a statement released to Canadian media. "To lose him in such a preventable, violent way is unbearable. We expect both the Canadian and Mexican governments to thoroughly investigate this operator so no other family has to go through this nightmare."

### International response and consular aid

Government officials in Washington, Ottawa, and Mexico City expressed deep condolences on Wednesday as consular teams mobilized to assist the victims and their families.

A US State Department spokesperson confirmed that at least six American citizens were killed and seven others were hospitalized. 

"We extend our deepest condolences to the families of those who died in this tragic bus accident," the spokesperson said. "Our embassy and consular teams in Mexico are providing all possible consular assistance, including coordinating with local medical authorities and facilitating the repatriation of remains."

Global Affairs Canada confirmed that four Canadian citizens were among the deceased and two were injured. Canadian officials said consular team members have been deployed to the region to provide on-the-ground support to impacted families.

Quintana Roo Governor Mara Lezama expressed her condolences in a video message posted to social media, promising full transparency and support for the victims' families.

"Our hearts go out to the families who have lost loved ones in this deeply tragic event," Lezama said. "We are committed to providing medical care to the injured, full support to the families affected, and a rigorous investigation to determine full accountability."

Authorities said seven victims remain hospitalized with severe injuries, including head trauma and orthopedic fractures. Names of the deceased are expected to be officially released once all next of kin have been notified.

**SALTILLO, Mexico (CNN)** -- A head-on collision between a heavy tractor-trailer and a charter tourist bus on a fog-shrouded highway in northern Mexico left at least 14 people dead and 22 others injured early Thursday, Mexican authorities said.

The crash occurred shortly after 6:00 a.m. local time on Federal Highway 57, a major transport artery connecting the industrial city of Monclova to Saltillo, the capital of Coahuila state. 

According to Coahuila State Civil Protection spokesman Roberto De León, the semi-truck—carrying several tons of rolled steel—appeared to lose control while negotiating a curve, crossing the central median into oncoming traffic and slamming directly into the passenger bus.

The force of the impact tore open the left side of the bus and sent both vehicles skidding down a steep embankment into a rocky ravine. 

**[WATCH: Rescuers cut through wreckage to reach survivors (1:45)]**
**[WATCH: Local official describes 'chaotic' scene on Highway 57 (2:12)]**

"The destruction is catastrophic," De León said in a phone interview from the scene. "It took emergency crews nearly three hours using hydraulic rescue tools just to stabilize the bus chassis and reach those trapped inside."

At least eight of the deceased were pronounced dead at the scene, while six others died en route to or shortly after arriving at hospitals in Saltillo and nearby Ramos Arizpe, medical personnel confirmed. 

### Texas retirees among victims

The charter bus, operated by *Turismo Del Norte*, was carrying 38 passengers on a seven-day historical tour of northern Mexico. Emergency responders confirmed that several American citizens were on board.

Among those killed were Mark and Linda Hollingsworth of San Antonio, Texas. The couple, both 62, were celebrating their 40th wedding anniversary, according to family members back home.

"They loved traveling, especially by motorcoach so they could see the countryside," said their daughter, Sarah Miller, speaking from her home in Austin. "My dad called me from the hotel last night saying how excited they were to see the historic district in Saltillo. We just can't believe they're gone."

Also identified among the deceased was the bus driver, 44-year-old Alejandro Treviño of Monterrey, a father of three who had driven tour routes in northern Mexico for over 15 years. 

**[RELATED: Map showing location of Coahuila crash site]**

The driver of the semi-truck survived the crash with severe injuries and remains under police guard at a Saltillo trauma center. Authorities said an investigation is underway to determine if driver fatigue, excessive speed, or mechanical failure contributed to the accident. Heavy morning fog and wet pavement were also reported at the time of the crash.

### Consular assistance deployed

The U.S. Consulate in Monterrey issued a statement Thursday afternoon saying officials are working closely with Mexican authorities to identify any additional American casualties and assist grieving relatives.

"Our thoughts and prayers are with the victims and their families during this tragic time," the statement read. "Consular officers are on the ground in Coahuila providing all possible consular assistance."

Survivors rushed to regional hospitals reported scenes of sudden terror as the collision occurred.

"Most people were sleeping," said David Morales, 29, a passenger from Nuevo Laredo who escaped with a fractured collarbone and severe cuts. "There was a loud horn, the sound of screeching metal, and then total darkness. People were screaming for help in the dark."

Traffic along Highway 57 remained halted for over six hours Thursday as federal police cleared heavy debris and hazardous steel rolls scattered across the lanes.

For Sofia Ramos-Miller, 38, of Des Moines, Iowa, the horror began with a phone call she missed at 4:15 a.m.

"Someone made a selfish, disgusting choice to get behind the wheel drunk," Sofia said, her grief turning to anger. "In five seconds, that person destroyed twelve families. ### A Long Road to Healing

Cross-border bus routes like the one from McAllen to Zacatecas are vital lifelines for the Mexican-American diaspora, carrying thousands of workers, parents, and children back and forth across the border every week to maintain ties with their homeland.

As the suspect awaits formal charges in a Nuevo León jail, families in Mexico and across the United States are left to pick up the pieces.

**At least 8 dead, 15 injured after tour bus carrying US tourists crashes in northeast Mexico, officials say**

**By CNN Staff**
*Updated 1:45 PM EDT, Tuesday*

**MONTERREY, Mexico (CNN) —** At least eight people are dead and 15 others injured after a tour bus carrying American tourists primarily from Texas and Iowa collided with a commercial truck in northeast Mexico early Tuesday morning, local emergency officials said.

The crash occurred around 5:30 a.m. local time along Federal Highway 85 near the municipality of Linares, in the state of Nuevo León, approximately 80 miles south of Monterrey. 

According to Nuevo León Civil Protection, the charter bus was en route after crossing the U.S.-Mexico border, traveling toward central Mexico, when it struck a jackknifed tractor-trailer. Authorities noted that heavy morning fog severely reduced visibility on the stretch of highway at the time of the collision.

Six victims were pronounced dead at the scene, while two others succumbed to their injuries shortly after arriving at a regional hospital in Linares, authorities said. Five of the 15 injured passengers remain in critical condition.

State officials confirmed that the bus was transporting a private tour group consisting of 26 passengers, including several families from Texas and a church group from Iowa. 

"Visibility was extremely limited due to dense fog along the corridor," said Erik Cavazos, director of Nuevo León Civil Protection, during a press briefing. "Emergency crews from multiple municipalities worked for hours using hydraulic equipment to extricate passengers who were trapped inside the vehicle."

Several of the most critically injured passengers were airlifted by medical helicopters to University Hospital in Monterrey, state health officials confirmed.

A U.S. Department of State spokesperson confirmed to CNN that consular officials are actively responding to the incident.

"We can confirm the deaths and injuries of U.S. citizens in a road accident in Nuevo León, Mexico," the spokesperson said. "Personnel from the U.S. Consulate General in Monterrey are on the ground providing consular assistance to the victims and their families. We extend our deepest condolences to the families of those who lost their lives."

Governor offices in both Texas and Iowa issued preliminary statements Tuesday morning expressing sorrow and stating they are coordinating with federal authorities to support the affected families. 

The cause of the crash remains under investigation by the Mexican Federal Highway Police and the Nuevo León Attorney General's Office. Both the bus driver and the driver of the tractor-trailer survived the impact with non-life-threatening injuries and are currently in stable condition under police supervision as investigators work to determine liability.

Federal Highway 85, a vital commercial and transit artery connecting the U.S. border town of Laredo to central Mexico, was closed in both directions for more than six hours as emergency crews cleared debris and federal investigators documented the scene. Traffic has since been restored to a single lane.

*This is a developing story and will be updated.*
